subject: storytime
title: The Enormous Turnip
about: The Russian folk tale of a turnip so enormous that Grandpa, Grandma, a girl, a dog, a cat and at last a tiny mouse all have to pull together to get it out of the ground. The chain repeats and grows by one helper at a time, which makes it easy to read along, to retell in order and to see the lesson that even the smallest helper counts. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Line up stuffed animals and act it out, adding one helper at a time until the turnip pops out.

book.author: a folk tale from Russia (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A turnip so big that it takes everyone, even a mouse, to pull it up.

passage.text:
Grandpa planted a turnip seed.
"Grow, little turnip, grow!" he said.
"Grow big and sweet!"
The turnip grew and grew.
It grew big.
It grew bigger.
It grew enormous!
One day, Grandpa went to pull it up.
***
Grandpa pulled and pulled.
But the turnip did not come up.
He called Grandma to help.
Grandma pulled Grandpa.
Grandpa pulled the turnip.
They pulled and pulled.
But the turnip did not come up.
Grandma called the girl to help.
***
The girl pulled Grandma.
Grandma pulled Grandpa.
Grandpa pulled the turnip.
They pulled and pulled.
But the turnip did not come up.
The girl called the dog to help.
The dog pulled the girl.
The girl pulled Grandma.
Grandma pulled Grandpa.
Grandpa pulled the turnip.
They pulled and pulled.
But the turnip did not come up.
***
The dog called the cat to help.
The cat pulled the dog.
The dog pulled the girl.
The girl pulled Grandma.
Grandma pulled Grandpa.
Grandpa pulled the turnip.
They pulled and pulled.
But the turnip did not come up!
The cat called a little mouse.
"I can help!" said the mouse.
***
The mouse pulled the cat.
The cat pulled the dog.
The dog pulled the girl.
The girl pulled Grandma.
Grandma pulled Grandpa.
Grandpa pulled the turnip.
They pulled and pulled and pulled.
Pop!
Up came the turnip!
They all fell down in a heap.
"I helped!" said the little mouse.
That night, they all had turnip soup.
Even the smallest helper matters.

cards.note: A turnip is a round root vegetable that grows under the ground, like a carrot.
The mouse is the smallest helper of all, and she comes last.

cards.q: What did they all have that night?
cards.note: Turnips are often cooked in soups and stews.

cards.q: What happened when the turnip came up?
cards.note: Everyone tumbled into a heap, so act it out with a tug and a soft landing on a pillow.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: A seed, then an enormous turnip, then one helper after another.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: It took every helper, right down to the mouse, to pull it out.

cards.q: How did the mouse feel when the turnip came up?
cards.note: The mouse shouts that she helped, so ask him about a time he helped with a big job.
The turnip only came up when the tiny mouse joined in.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'enormous' mean?
cards.note: Enormous is even bigger than big, so stretch your arms as wide as they will go.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
